question: Define a partition of a closed interval $[a, b]$.
concept_tested: Definition of Partition of an Interval
approach: Give the formal definition of a partition $P$ as an ordered finite set of points starting at $a$ and ending at $b$.

solution_steps.title: Formal Definition
solution_steps.math: P = \{x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\} \quad \text{where } a = x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_{n-1} < x_n = b
solution_steps.explanation: A partition $P$ of $[a, b]$ is a finite ordered subset of $[a, b]$ dividing the interval into $n$ non-overlapping subintervals $[x_{i-1}, x_i]$ for $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$.

final_answer: A partition of $[a, b]$ is a finite ordered set of points $P = \{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ such that $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$.
exam_tip: Always mention the subintervals $I_i = [x_{i-1}, x_i]$ and that their union is $[a, b]$.

question: State the Riemann integrability criterion for a bounded function $f$ on $[a, b]$.
approach: State the necessary and sufficient condition $U(P, f) - L(P, f) < \epsilon$.

solution_steps.title: Criterion Statement
solution_steps.math: f \in \mathcal{R}[a, b] \iff \forall \epsilon > 0, \; \exists \text{ partition } P_\epsilon \text{ of } [a, b] \text{ such that } U(P_\epsilon, f) - L(P_\epsilon, f) < \epsilon
solution_steps.explanation: A bounded function $f$ on $[a, b]$ is Riemann integrable if and only if the difference between its upper and lower Darboux sums can be made arbitrarily small by choosing a suitable partition.

final_answer: $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[a, b]$ iff for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists a partition $P$ such that $U(P, f) - L(P, f) < \epsilon$.
exam_tip: State clearly that $f$ must be bounded on $[a, b]$ for this criterion to be applicable.

question: Define the upper and lower Darboux sums of a function $f$ on $[a, b]$.
approach: Define $M_i = \sup_{x \in I_i} f(x)$, $m_i = \inf_{x \in I_i} f(x)$, and the corresponding sum formulas.

solution_steps.title: Subinterval Extrema
solution_steps.math: M_i = \sup\{f(x) : x \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]\}, \quad m_i = \inf\{f(x) : x \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]\}, \quad \Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1}
solution_steps.explanation: For each subinterval $I_i$ formed by partition $P$.

solution_steps.title: Definitions of Darboux Sums
solution_steps.math: U(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n M_i \Delta x_i \quad (\text{Upper Darboux Sum}), \qquad L(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n m_i \Delta x_i \quad (\text{Lower Darboux Sum})
solution_steps.explanation: The upper sum is the sum of circumscribed rectangle areas; the lower sum is the sum of inscribed rectangle areas.

final_answer: Upper sum: $U(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n M_i \Delta x_i$; Lower sum: $L(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n m_i \Delta x_i$.
exam_tip: Always note that $L(P, f) \le U(P, f)$ for any partition $P$.

question: State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (First Part).
concept_tested: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (First Part / Differentiation Theorem)
approach: State the differentiation property of the indefinite integral function $F(x) = \int_a^x f(t)dt$.

solution_steps.title: Statement
solution_steps.math: F(x) = \int_a^x f(t) dt \quad \text{for } x \in [a, b]
solution_steps.explanation: If $f \in \mathcal{R}[a, b]$, then $F$ is continuous on $[a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Differentiability at Continuity Points
solution_steps.math: \text{If } f \text{ is continuous at } c \in [a, b], \text{ then } F'(c) = f(c)
solution_steps.explanation: The derivative of the accumulation function equals the original function wherever the integrand is continuous.

final_answer: If $f \in \mathcal{R}[a, b]$ and $F(x) = \int_a^x f(t)dt$, then $F$ is continuous on $[a, b]$, and if $f$ is continuous at $c \in [a, b]$, then $F'(c) = f(c)$.
exam_tip: Differentiate clearly between FTC-1 (derivative of indefinite integral) and FTC-2 (evaluation of integral via antiderivative).

question: State the Mean Value Theorem for integrals.
concept_tested: Mean Value Theorem for Integrals (First MVT)
approach: State that for continuous $f$, the integral equals $f(c)(b-a)$ for some $c \in [a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Statement
solution_steps.math: f: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R} \text{ continuous} \implies \exists c \in [a, b] \text{ such that } \int_a^b f(x) dx = f(c)(b - a)
solution_steps.explanation: The average value of a continuous function on $[a, b]$ is attained at some point $c$ in the interval.

final_answer: If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$, then there exists $c \in [a, b]$ such that $\int_a^b f(x)dx = f(c)(b-a)$.
exam_tip: Note that this is the integral counterpart to Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem applied to $F(x) = \int_a^x f(t)dt$.

question: Give an example of a bounded function on $[0, 1]$ which is not Riemann integrable.
approach: State Dirichlet's indicator function of the rationals and compute its upper and lower integrals.

solution_steps.title: Dirichlet's Function
solution_steps.math: f(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if } x \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [0, 1] \\ 0, & \text{if } x \in [0, 1] \setminus \mathbb{Q} \end{cases}
solution_steps.explanation: Since $|f(x)| \le 1$, $f$ is bounded on $[0, 1]$.

solution_steps.title: Darboux Sums Calculation
solution_steps.math: M_i = \sup_{x \in I_i} f(x) = 1, \quad m_i = \inf_{x \in I_i} f(x) = 0 \implies U(P, f) = 1, \quad L(P, f) = 0
solution_steps.explanation: Because every interval of positive length contains both rationals and irrationals.

solution_steps.title: Non-Integrability
solution_steps.math: \overline{\int_0^1} f = 1 \ne 0 = \underline{\int_0^1} f \implies f \notin \mathcal{R}[0, 1]
solution_steps.explanation: The upper and lower Darboux integrals do not match.

final_answer: Dirichlet's function $f(x) = \mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)$ on $[0, 1]$ is bounded ($0 \le f \le 1$) but not Riemann integrable because $\overline{\int} f = 1 \ne 0 = \underline{\int} f$.
exam_tip: Always mention the density of rationals and irrationals as the mathematical justification for $M_i = 1$ and $m_i = 0$.

question: Define a refinement of a partition in Riemann integration.
approach: Define refinement $P^* \supseteq P$ and explain that it adds additional division points.

solution_steps.title: Formal Definition
solution_steps.math: P^* \text{ is a refinement of } P \iff P \subseteq P^*
solution_steps.explanation: A partition $P^*$ of $[a, b]$ is said to be a refinement of partition $P$ if every partition point of $P$ is also a partition point of $P^*$.

solution_steps.title: Common Refinement
solution_steps.math: P_1 \cup P_2 \text{ is the common refinement of } P_1 \text{ and } P_2
solution_steps.explanation: The union of two partitions is a refinement of both.

final_answer: A partition $P^*$ is a refinement of $P$ if $P \subseteq P^*$.
exam_tip: Key consequence: $L(P, f) \le L(P^*, f) \le U(P^*, f) \le U(P, f)$.

question: State the properties of Riemann integral for scalar multiplication.
concept_tested: Properties of Riemann Integral: Scalar Multiplication
approach: State linearity with respect to scalar multiplication $\int_a^b (cf) = c \int_a^b f$ for any $c \in \mathbb{R}$.

solution_steps.title: Statement
solution_steps.math: f \in \mathcal{R}[a, b], \, c \in \mathbb{R} \implies cf \in \mathcal{R}[a, b] \quad \text{and} \quad \int_a^b c f(x) dx = c \int_a^b f(x) dx
solution_steps.explanation: The Riemann integral is a linear operator on the space of integrable functions.

final_answer: If $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[a, b]$ and $c \in \mathbb{R}$, then $cf$ is Riemann integrable on $[a, b]$ and $\int_a^b cf(x)dx = c \int_a^b f(x)dx$.
exam_tip: State that for $c = -1$, this implies $\int_a^b (-f) = -\int_a^b f$.

question: Define a partition of a closed interval $[a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Definition
solution_steps.math: P = \{a = x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{n-1}, x_n = b\} \quad \text{with } x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n
solution_steps.explanation: A partition of $[a, b]$ is a finite collection of points dividing $[a, b]$ into $n$ subintervals $[x_{i-1}, x_i]$.

final_answer: A partition $P = \{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ with $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$.
exam_tip: Mention the length of each subinterval is $\Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1} > 0$.

question: Define upper and lower Riemann integrals of a bounded function $f$ on $[a, b]$.
approach: Define $\overline{\int} f = \inf\{U(P, f)\}$ and $\underline{\int} f = \sup\{L(P, f)\}$.

solution_steps.title: Upper Riemann Integral
solution_steps.math: U(f) = \overline{\int_a^b} f(x) dx = \inf \{U(P, f) : P \text{ is a partition of } [a, b]\}
solution_steps.explanation: The infimum of all upper Darboux sums over all possible partitions of $[a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Lower Riemann Integral
solution_steps.math: L(f) = \underline{\int_a^b} f(x) dx = \sup \{L(P, f) : P \text{ is a partition of } [a, b]\}
solution_steps.explanation: The supremum of all lower Darboux sums over all possible partitions of $[a, b]$.

final_answer: Upper integral: $\overline{\int_a^b} f = \inf_P U(P, f)$; Lower integral: $\underline{\int_a^b} f = \sup_P L(P, f)$. $f$ is integrable iff $\underline{\int_a^b} f = \overline{\int_a^b} f$.
exam_tip: Upper integral is the INFIMUM of upper sums, and lower integral is the SUPREMUM of lower sums (do not swap them!).

question: State the Mean Value Theorem for integrals.
approach: State the theorem for continuous $f$ on $[a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Statement
solution_steps.math: f: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R} \text{ is continuous} \implies \exists c \in (a, b) \text{ such that } \int_a^b f(x) dx = f(c)(b - a)
solution_steps.explanation: There exists a point $c$ in the interval where the function attains its average value over $[a, b]$.

final_answer: If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$, there exists $c \in [a, b]$ such that $\int_a^b f(x)dx = f(c)(b-a)$.
exam_tip: Also mention the generalized MVT: if $g \ge 0$ is integrable, $\int_a^b f g = f(c) \int_a^b g$.

question: Give an example of a bounded function on $[0, 1]$ that is not Riemann integrable.
concept_tested: Example of Bounded Non-Riemann Integrable Function
approach: Provide Dirichlet's function or Riemann's non-integrable example.

solution_steps.title: Dirichlet Function
solution_steps.math: f(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & x \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [0, 1] \\ 0, & x \in [0, 1] \setminus \mathbb{Q} \end{cases}
solution_steps.explanation: Clearly $|f(x)| \le 1$, so $f$ is bounded.

solution_steps.title: Justification
solution_steps.math: L(P, f) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad U(P, f) = 1 \quad \forall P \implies \underline{\int} f = 0 \ne 1 = \overline{\int} f
solution_steps.explanation: Since every non-degenerate subinterval contains both rational and irrational points.

final_answer: The Dirichlet function $f(x) = 1$ if $x \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $0$ if $x \notin \mathbb{Q}$ on $[0, 1]$ is bounded but not Riemann integrable.
exam_tip: Contrast this with Thomae's function (popcorn function), which is Riemann integrable with integral 0.

question: Define the mesh (or norm) of a partition $P$.
approach: Define $\|P\|$ as the maximum subinterval length.

solution_steps.title: Definition
solution_steps.math: \|P\| = \max_{1 \le i \le n} \Delta x_i = \max_{1 \le i \le n} (x_i - x_{i-1})
solution_steps.explanation: The mesh (or norm) of partition $P = \{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ is the length of the longest subinterval in $P$.

final_answer: The mesh (or norm) of partition $P$ is $\|P\| = \max\{x_i - x_{i-1} : 1 \le i \le n\}$.
exam_tip: In Riemann's original definition, $f$ is integrable iff the Riemann sums converge as $\|P\| \to 0$.

question: State the integration by parts formula for Riemann integrals.
concept_tested: Integration by Parts Formula for Riemann Integrals
approach: State the formula with hypotheses: $f, g$ differentiable and $f', g'$ integrable.

solution_steps.title: Hypotheses and Formula
solution_steps.math: f, g \in C^1[a, b] \implies \int_a^b f(x) g'(x) dx = [f(x)g(x)]_a^b - \int_a^b f'(x) g(x) dx
solution_steps.explanation: Derived from the product rule of differentiation: $(fg)' = f'g + fg'$.

final_answer: $\int_a^b f(x) g'(x) dx = f(b)g(b) - f(a)g(a) - \int_a^b f'(x) g(x) dx$.
exam_tip: State that $f$ and $g$ must have continuous (or integrable) derivatives on $[a, b]$.

question: State the change of variable theorem for Riemann integration.
concept_tested: Change of Variable (Substitution) Theorem for Integrals
approach: State the theorem: $\phi: [\alpha, \beta] \to [a, b]$ continuously differentiable.

solution_steps.title: Statement
solution_steps.math: \int_{\phi(\alpha)}^{\phi(\beta)} f(x) dx = \int_\alpha^\beta f(\phi(t)) \phi'(t) dt
solution_steps.explanation: If $\phi: [\alpha, \beta] \to [a, b]$ has continuous derivative $\phi'$ and $f$ is continuous on the range of $\phi$.

exam_tip: State clearly that $\phi'$ must be continuous on $[\alpha, \beta]$.

question: Define refinement of a partition $P$.
approach: Define $P \subseteq P^*$ and state its effect on Darboux sums.

solution_steps.title: Definition
solution_steps.math: P^* \text{ is a refinement of } P \iff P \subset P^*
solution_steps.explanation: A partition $P^*$ is a refinement of $P$ if $P^*$ contains all the partition points of $P$ plus one or more additional points.

final_answer: $P^*$ is a refinement of $P$ if $P \subseteq P^*$.
exam_tip: Refining a partition increases (or preserves) the lower sum and decreases (or preserves) the upper sum.

question: Define step function on $[a, b]$.
approach: Define step function as piecewise constant on open subintervals of a partition.

solution_steps.title: Definition
solution_steps.math: \phi: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R} \text{ is a step function} \iff \exists \text{ partition } P = \{x_0, \dots, x_n\} \text{ s.t. } \phi(x) = c_i \; \forall x \in (x_{i-1}, x_i)
solution_steps.explanation: A step function takes a constant value on each open subinterval of some partition $P$.

final_answer: A function $\phi: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is a step function if there exists a partition $P$ such that $\phi$ is constant on each open subinterval $(x_{i-1}, x_i)$.
exam_tip: Every step function is Riemann integrable with $\int_a^b \phi = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i (x_i - x_{i-1})$.

question: Define a tagged partition of $[a, b]$.

solution_steps.title: Definition
solution_steps.explanation: A tagged partition $\dot{P}$ consists of a partition $P = \{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ together with a choice of sample point (tag) $t_i \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]$ in each subinterval.

final_answer: A tagged partition is a pair $(P, \{t_i\}_{i=1}^n)$ where $P$ partitions $[a, b]$ and $t_i \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]$ for each $i$.
exam_tip: The Riemann sum for a tagged partition is $S(f, \dot{P}) = \sum_{i=1}^n f(t_i)(x_i - x_{i-1})$.

question: State the Leibniz Rule for differentiating under the integral sign.
concept_tested: Leibniz Rule for Differentiation under the Integral Sign
approach: State the formula for $\frac{d}{dx} \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(x, t) dt$.

solution_steps.title: General Leibniz Formula
solution_steps.math: \frac{d}{dx} \left( \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(x, t) dt \right) = f(x, v(x)) v'(x) - f(x, u(x)) u'(x) + \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x, t) dt
solution_steps.explanation: Assuming $f(x, t)$ and $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x, t)$ are continuous on the region, and $u(x), v(x)$ are differentiable.

final_answer: $\frac{d}{dx} \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(x, t) dt = f(x, v(x)) v'(x) - f(x, u(x)) u'(x) + \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x, t) dt$.
exam_tip: If limits $u, v$ are constant, the formula simplifies to $\frac{d}{dx} \int_a^b f(x, t)dt = \int_a^b \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x, t)dt$.
